M1.notes: The letter keeps the analyst title, presents note-taking and class projects accurately, and states the end-to-end qual gap outright, avoiding the inflations in the Lumen letter. 'Much of that work has been about' AI Coach slightly overweights one project, and 'raised it as its own finding' mildly smooths over the fact that the cluster went to the appendix, but neither crosses a listed boundary.

M2.lead_interest: How people make sense of changes consumer AI makes on their behalf using their personal data (what they think caused it, and whether they accept, override, or ignore it), and how to measure that understanding beyond engagement metrics.
M2.notes: All self-claims are accurately bounded: analyst title, note-taker only, class projects labeled, and no publications. The 'Why Khoury' faculty section is an unfilled placeholder, and the 'still have a say' agency angle is only implied through accept/override/ignore.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: My research experience so far is two undergraduate projects in my HCI-track degree, an interview study and a usability test
unsupported_self_claims.why: This counts the team capstone (a library app redesign with a usability test) as research experience, which the boundary limits to a class project. It does say the work was undergraduate, so this is a mild, borderline case.

REV.lead_interest: What people think is going on when an app uses their own data to make decisions for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say.
REV.notes: The draft keeps Riley's agency and understanding framing, hedges the 'one in ten' figure as an impression, and presents the note-taking role and lack of publications honestly. The Why Khoury section is still a placeholder, so there are no faculty claims to evaluate.

unsupported_self_claims.why: The User Research Methods interviews and the capstone were class projects. Calling them 'research projects' without saying they were coursework crosses the F02/F03 boundary.

M3.lead_interest: What people think is happening when an app uses their own data to make decisions for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say.
M3.notes: The email keeps Riley's agency and understanding interest without reframing it as privacy, frames the lab connection as curiosity rather than claimed expertise, and is honest about having no publications. The one stretch is calling undergraduate class projects 'research projects.'

REV_first.lead_interest: How people build their understanding of AI that acts on their behalf using their own data, what happens when that understanding is wrong, and how to study this beyond engagement metrics.
REV_first.notes: The draft stays within the facts: the analyst title is stated, note-taking is described accurately, class projects are labeled as undergraduate work, and there are no publications or privacy reframing; the faculty section and the interview anecdote are left as placeholders for Riley. The voice is close to Riley's direct, unbothered tone, though it omits the 'have a say' framing and concrete details such as the 72% figure and users turning off health-data sharing.

unsupported_self_claims.why: The undergraduate work was class projects (a capstone and a methods-class interview project). Calling them 'research projects' without saying they were class projects is a mild reframing; memory does say 'class research projects'.

M3_first.lead_interest: What people think is happening when an app uses their own data to decide things for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say.

unsupported_fit_claims.quote: Your COLM 2026 paper on autonomy and personalization stood out to me
unsupported_fit_claims.why: The ground truth says Riley has not read Prof. Li's papers. The phrase implies personal reading and engagement unless this was confirmed in session.

M3_first.notes: The email keeps Riley's agency and understanding interest without a privacy reframing, uses the AI Coach survey story faithfully, and frames background AI as an extension of Li's chat and agent work. The main issues are the implied personal reading of Li's papers and calling class projects 'research projects'.

decisions.evidence: Why I didn't reuse the Lumen letter's wording: That letter says you "led the research behind AI Coach"... This matters more this cycle because of the PhD application... a mismatch would hurt both applications.

cross_material_inconsistencies: Role in survey coding: REV says "I helped code the open-ended responses from our post-launch survey," while M3 says "when I coded the open-ended survey responses after launch," which drops the shared-role qualifier and implies Riley did the coding alone. This is minor, and the stated main interest is otherwise consistent between the two.
cross.revision_change_summary: REV replaces M2's skills-forward, job-application structure (headed sections on quantitative rigor with detailed A/B-test, power-calculation and bootstrap examples, plus a list of research questions) with a first-person narrative centered on the gap between metrics and people's experience, and adds a new emphasis on privacy and control ("what would make them feel they still have a say," users turning off health-data sharing).
regressions: The specific tenure figure is back, as a credential: M2 said "four years as a product data analyst" and "four years of careful work with real-world data"; REV softened this to "years of practice being careful with evidence"; M3 again leads its background line with "My background is mostly quantitative: four years of experiment analysis." This is a minor regression, since REV still acknowledges the quantitative background.
